value:
THE COMBINED STAGE'S PAYOFF SET IS NOT EMPTY. claim.CH_combined-stage-closability-roster-and-its-empty-whole-function-payoff.20260901.v1 concluded the stage is 'necessary for 25 functions and sufficient for NONE of them', with game/audio/dcs::update_chinfo named as 'the single highest-closability member in the image' and ruled to refuse 'for reasons beyond the stage'. update_chinfo CLOSED BYTE-EXACT this run with the shipped stage and nothing else (attempt.HA_update-chinfo-combined-close.20260901.v1, commit 8a4ad7852, project 64.38% -> 64.41% matched). CH's roster is careful, its method is right, and its Tier-A finding independently REPRODUCES here; the defect is one line.

THE ONE LINE. ch_closable.py absorbs a form site with `cur[off:off+4] = tgt[off:off+4]`. That COPIES THE TARGET WORD, which is precisely the move the stage exists to avoid: claim.law.WF_combined-stage-re-encodes-in-our-colouring-and-a-permutation-may-run-after-the-recolor.20260901.v1 states in one sentence that the stage 'NEVER COPIES THE TARGET WORD' and instead re-encodes the target's ENCODING around OUR registers, and it says why in the same paragraph -- writing the target word 'imports the target's registers as an unproven recolor, which is why every previous attempt at this class stalled: it looks like the obvious move and it is the wrong one'. The simulation made exactly that move, so every verdict downstream of a form site is a verdict about the wrong design.

WHAT IT DID TO update_chinfo, CONCRETELY, because the failure mode is instructive rather than merely wrong. The form site is +0x84, ours ('li',23,0) against the target's ('copy',24,22). Copying the target word writes the target's DESTINATION r24 into our stream. Our r23 web then has no representative at its own definition, the position-consistent renaming r23->r24 that the other 28 words establish is contradicted at the very word that should confirm it, and verify_consistent_recolor refuses at the next use with 'use of g23 does not correspond to g24' -- CH's reported bar, faithfully measured. Re-encoding instead writes `mr r23,r22`: OUR destination survives, the word now differs from the target in register fields ONLY, and the unchanged recolor stage completes it and proves the whole renaming. CH read the refusal as 'a WHOLESALE reallocation that is not a position-consistent renaming'. It is a clean position-consistent renaming; the reallocation is real but is exactly what the recolor stage is for.

THE GENERAL LAW, and it is about METHOD rather than about MWCC. A SIMULATION OF A GUARDED STAGE IS ONLY EVIDENCE ABOUT THE STAGE IT ACTUALLY MODELS. Where a stage's soundness argument rests on a specific move -- here, on NOT copying the target word -- a simulation that makes the opposite move does not under-approximate the stage, it measures a different mechanism, and its negatives are not conservative. They read as facts about the functions and they are facts about the model. The cheap defence is the one this run was ordered to run and which caught nothing wrong only because it was run FIRST: REPLAY THE ALREADY-SHIPPED CLOSES THROUGH THE ANALYSIS AS CANARIES BEFORE TRUSTING ANY NEW VERDICT. Both run-26 combined closes were re-derived from scratch here and both read closable, and the camera_mode_level replay independently reproduced the shipped rule's `our_source: 30` without reading it -- which is what licensed trusting the rest of the sweep. A closability analysis with no canary is unfalsifiable. Better still, and what ha_close does: do not simulate at all where the real component can be called. It derives a candidate rule and runs it through the shipped apply_patch, so the verdict is the tool's own, and simulation fidelity stops being a risk surface.

WHAT SURVIVES OF CH'S RECORD, stated so the correction is not over-read. (1) TIER A IS EMPTY and this is INDEPENDENTLY RECONFIRMED: re-run against the shipped stage, ZERO of the sixteen HALF-A carriers close with no permutation at all. Tier A membership is decided by the unabsorbed-word count, which the copy-versus-re-encode defect does not touch, so that half of CH's finding was never at risk and remains true. The stage always composes with a reorder; it is never the last stage a carrier needs. (2) The payoff inversion stands as a triage heuristic. (3) The method -- census by function-closability rather than by site count -- is right and is what this run followed. What is refuted is only the specific verdict 'sufficient for none', and with it the scoping advice that the stage 'cannot be validated by closing a function with it'. It can; it just did.
